_note: The root craft: 2 stones and 3 hours of grinding after discovering the cliff; personal completion unlocks descendants even when another sharp tool is already owned.

log: Holding one stone against another, you patiently grind away the rough surface until a usable cutting edge emerges.
Three hours of grinding stone on stone. The edge is rough, but it cuts.
You first detach flakes with sharp blows, then refine the edge by grinding.
You hack the straightest branch to a point with the rock knife.
The rock knife chews more than it cuts, but at last the branch has a point.
Stroke after stroke with the stone blade, until the tip is sharp enough.
You choose the straightest branch and carve it to a point with the knife.
You pick the straightest branch and whittle the tip sharp.
Shaving by shaving, the knife turns a branch into a point.

_note: needs something sharp: the knife 30 min; the rock knife is slower (its tool.hoursFactor 2), with its own texts

log: You strike a hard stone until it bears a cutting edge, then secure it tightly in a split wooden haft.
Stone on stone until one has an edge.
A sharp stone, a stout branch, and a long time binding them.
You lash a flat stone across the end of a log handle.
A flat stone, a handle cut from a log, a lot of cord.
You bind a flat stone crosswise to a handle. A hoe, of sorts.

_note: Four bark strips twisted into rope; personal rock knife completion unlocks the recipe.

log: You twist strips of inner bark into three strands, then lay the strands together to obtain a stronger rope.
Hour after hour the fibres are braided until a length of serviceable rope lies coiled at your feet.
Strip by strip, the bark becomes cord, and the cord a rope. Your fingers ache.
